review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Separate selected state, process, event, relation and property senses; expand sleep and mood; distinguish a vocal action from its sound and trudging from raving.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. NIH supports human sleep phase distinctions; Russian dictionary entries and Cambridge support selected verb senses. Qualified labels and graph mappings are editorial adaptations, not copied definitions.
review.context_policy: All new concepts and assertions use U1 with unspecified strength. Existing home contexts and upper exclusions remain unchanged. Process/state classification is a local ontology decision and is not presented as a universal lexical distinction.

sense_decisions.scope: A condition of mental functioning, classified as a state rather than a mental process.

sense_decisions.alignment: state sense mapped to local ontology
sense_decisions.scope: A mental condition with an emotional character; distinguish it from the process and adjective-property axes.
A mental property characterizing emotion or mood; cheerfulness and sadness are not moral virtues or faults.
A mood characterized by cheerfulness; a state bearing a property rather than a subtype of that property.
A mood characterized by sadness; not a diagnosis or a moral failing.
A condition of a body or bodily functioning; separate from the physiological process family.
The condition of being asleep, distinct from sleeping as an unfolding physiological process. Do not import absolute absence of awareness.
The transition from sleep to wakefulness, not metaphorical awareness or a religious movement.
The sleepy condition or tendency to fall asleep; it does not imply that sleep has already begun.
A short episode of sleeping, with no fixed duration, time of day or requirement to be outside a bed.
Sleeping during the relevant daytime period; it need not be brief.
The intersection of short duration and daytime occurrence; neither restriction alone entails the other.
Sleeping by a human, providing an explicit scope for the following clinical sleep-phase vocabulary.
Human sleeping during the rapid-eye-movement phase; a phase-restricted sleeping process, not the entire sleep cycle.
Human sleeping during the non-REM phase, with the three stages distinguished by the subject source.
Human non-REM sleeping during stage 1, at the transition from wakefulness.
Human non-REM sleeping during stage 2; no fixed duration, frequency or diagnostic condition is encoded.
Human non-REM sleeping during the deep, slow-wave stage; it is narrower than non-REM sleep overall.
The duration of a sleeping episode; a quantity distinct from the process, state and occupied time interval.
Measurement of how long a sleeping episode lasts; no target value or health recommendation.
The perceived howl produced by a person or animal, distinct from producing it. Exclude analogous wind and machinery sounds.

sense_decisions.alignment: restricted Russian verb sense; not exact OEWN rave alignment
sense_decisions.scope: Incoherent vocal speech in a partly uncontrolled or altered state; this lexical behavior is not itself a medical diagnosis. Exclude enthusiastic praise and figurative obsession.
Cambridge rave supports uncontrolled speech, but is broader. The qualified English phrase selects the archived Russian vocal meaning; no exact synonymy with all rave senses is asserted.
Preserve all inherited bearer, purpose, study and sleep/fatigue edges. Separating the state does not newly validate inherited probability percentages.
Preserve walking and its two explicit negative animal capabilities; broad motion-verb aliases need a later review.
Reuse vocalization and preserve singing and sound-production links.
Reuse the existing waking state rather than adding an English-word duplicate.
Reuse the existing dozing state; add sleepiness separately because feeling sleepy does not entail sleep.
Reuse the vocal action and create only its distinct perceived result.
Reuse mood and introduce an explicit emotional-state family; grammatical mood remains outside scope.

review.limits: No diagnosis, treatment, sleep-duration recommendation, mandatory stage sequence or claim that dreaming occurs only in REM. Human phase restrictions are not projected onto every animal. The wider emotion, sound, motion and state hierarchies remain only partly reviewed. Historical probabilities, including sleep/fatigue claims, remain untouched and are not newly endorsed. No application test suites.

split_archive.decision: Retain the walking sense at 19387 and add a separate vocal raving sense. Generated ambiguous lookup forms are removed, without claiming that every historical use of the noun is invalid.

exclusion_review.decision: Remove incompatible mixed-sense genus assertions, never the upper exclusions themselves. Preserve all explicit negations. Zero shared-descendant witnesses is not full validation of every inherited edge.

review.collision_decision: One intentional sense relocation: Russian бредить replaces the mistagged БРЕДИТЬ at the archived mixed walking record. No matching alias remains there after the planned removal. All other new terms have no normalized baseline collision. Reuse sleep process, mood, wakefulness, sleep onset, dozing, walking, vocalization and vocal howling.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.

repairs.reason: The selected cheerful adjective denotes an emotional property, not a moral quality. OEWN 2025: oewn-00363547-a.
A cheerful property is not an emotion process; the corresponding mood is represented separately.
The selected sad adjective denotes an emotional property, not a moral quality. OEWN 2025: oewn-01364779-a.
Mood is a feeling state in this local ontology; the inherited emotion parent is a mental process. OEWN 2025: oewn-07566518-n.
Do not classify the sleeping process simultaneously as a state. The distinct state is newly represented without redirecting the existing process facts.
Wakefulness in the selected sense is the condition of being awake, not the act of waking. OEWN 2025: oewn-05686315-n.

The selected dozing state is a light-sleep state. The lexicon also offers a process sense, which is not imported here. Source: https://sensefreq.ruslang.ru/w/RNC%20(verbs)/%D0%B4%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B0%D1%82%D1%8C
Producing a vocal howl is a vocalization, not a subtype of the sound property. OEWN 2025: oewn-01048804-v.
A sudden vocal howl is a restricted howling action. It need not be an intentional communication.
The action producing the howl is not itself a sound property.
The selected trudging motion is walking; use the existing nearer genus. OEWN 2025: oewn-01925197-v. Source: https://gramota.ru/poisk?mode=slovari&query=%D1%80%D0%B5%D1%81%D1%82%D0%B8&simple=0
The walking verb брести was conflated with бредить; do not infer a physiological-process genus from that second verb.
Being subject to selects an existing relation sense, not a separate state genus. Preserve relation edge 6597.
The selected hidden state is not the physical action of hiding; preserve the existing state genus.
Disputing a claim is a communicative action, not a state.
According someone an honor or attention selects a social action, not the resulting state.
Remaining in a condition is not necessarily a social action; the selected state meaning also applies to inanimate things. Source: https://slovar.cc/rus/efremova/220076.html

The selected occurrence belongs to the event family in this ontology. OEWN 2025: oewn-00340744-v. Source: https://gramota.ru/poisk?mode=all&query=%D1%81%D0%BE%D1%81%D1%82%D0%BE%D1%8F%D1%82%D1%81%D1%8F&simple=0
An event taking place is not the state of an entity.
